GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs is a high-quality franchise with genuine earnings momentum — Q1 2026 EPS +24.3% YoY, ROE expanding from 12.0% to 14.7%, investment banking revenue up 48% YoY, and a record backlog. The strategic re-centering away from consumer banking toward core advisory and AWM strengths is sound. However, the stock has already re-rated aggressively: P/E has expanded from 13.2x to 17.2x (~30% multiple expansion) and P/B from 1.58x to 2.53x (~60% expansion) over the past year, leaving limited upside from current levels. The SpaceX IPO mandate (20 May 2026) is a credible near-term catalyst that provides modest support, but the valuation already prices in much of the good news. Risks include cyclical revenue dependence, rising GSIB surcharges (50bps in 2026), and elevated leverage at 15.8x. Net: strong business, stretched entry price — mildly attractive with a catalyst bump.
key_factors: Q1 2026 EPS $17.55, +24.3% YoY; revenue $17.23B, +14.4% YoY, beating consensus of $16.66B
ROE improved to 14.7% from 12.0% YoY; operating margin stable at 37.7%
P/E at 17.2x near top of 365-day range (13.1x–18.4x); P/B at 2.53x at ceiling of range (1.6x–2.5x) — ~30% and ~60% multiple expansion respectively over past year
SpaceX IPO lead underwriter mandate (20 May 2026) — potential $1B+ in shared fees, stock popped 5.8% on news
Investment banking revenue surged 48% YoY to $2.84B; backlog at multi-year highs
GSIB surcharge expected to increase 50bps in Q1 2026 with possible additional 50bps in 2028 — capital headwind
Leverage at 15.8x (total liabilities $1,937.4B / equity $122.78B) — normal for G-SIB but limited stress buffer
Strategic re-centering: exit from consumer banking (Apple Card transition), focus on advisory, global markets, AWM fee-based growth
